animals.name: Blue jays
animals.fact: Blue jays eat acorns and may store some to eat later.

animals.name: Bottlenose dolphins
animals.fact: A bottlenose dolphin breathes through a blowhole on top of its head.

animals.name: Brown bears
animals.fact: Brown bears use strong claws to dig up food such as roots.
animals.sourceName: Alaska Department of Fish and Game

animals.name: Centipedes
animals.fact: A centipede has one pair of legs on each segment that carries legs.
animals.sourceName: University of California Statewide IPM Program

animals.name: Chickens
animals.fact: Chickens take dust baths to help keep clean.

animals.name: Dogs
animals.fact: Dogs have a well-developed sense of smell. Some working dogs learn to pick out a particular scent.
animals.sourceName: Cornell University College of Veterinary Medicine

animals.name: Elephants
animals.fact: An elephant’s trunk joins its nose and upper lip. The trunk has no bones.

animals.name: Giant panda
animals.fact: A special wrist bone helps a giant panda grip bamboo as it eats.

animals.name: Giraffes
animals.fact: Giraffes are the tallest animals that live on land.

animals.name: Mice
animals.fact: House mice use their whiskers to feel the surfaces they explore.

animals.name: Octopuses
animals.fact: An octopus has eight arms. The arms carry suckers that help it grip.

animals.name: Owls
animals.fact: Special feather edges help many owls fly with very little sound.

animals.name: Penguins
animals.fact: A penguin pushes through the water with its flippers and steers with its feet and tail.

animals.name: Rabbits and hares
animals.fact: Rabbits and hares can turn their long ears in different directions to listen.

animals.name: Sharks
animals.fact: A shark’s skeleton is made of cartilage, the same kind of flexible material found in the tip of your nose.

animals.name: Tigers
animals.fact: Each tiger has its own stripe pattern.

animals.name: Tree squirrels
animals.fact: Eastern gray squirrels bury food in little stores to eat through winter.

animals.name: Turtles
animals.fact: A turtle’s shell is part of its body. It is joined to its spine and ribs.

animals.name: Pigs
animals.fact: Pigs use their strong snouts to dig for food such as roots and insects.

animals.name: Red foxes
animals.fact: Red foxes can live in towns and cities. They use sheltered places for dens.

animals.name: Hedgehogs
animals.fact: A hedgehog can curl into a ball so its spines face outwards.

animals.name: Butterflies
animals.fact: A butterfly starts as an egg. It hatches into a caterpillar and changes into an adult inside a pupa.

animals.name: Bald eagles
animals.fact: Adult bald eagles have white feathers on their heads and tails. Young bald eagles start out mostly brown.

animals.name: Raccoons
animals.fact: A raccoon can sleep in a hollow tree, under a log or in an old burrow.

animals.name: Horses and ponies
animals.fact: A horse’s hooves keep growing, so a horse in human care needs regular hoof checks and trimming.

animals.name: Earthworms
animals.fact: Many earthworms live in soil and shelter in burrows. Some come up to the surface to move around.

animals.name: Leopards
animals.fact: A leopard’s long tail helps it balance on narrow branches.

animals.name: Ladybirds
animals.fact: Ladybirds are beetles. Many eat tiny plant-feeding insects called aphids.

animals.name: Lions
animals.fact: Lions can live in groups called prides. Lionesses in a pride often raise their cubs together.

animals.name: Deer
animals.fact: Deer that grow antlers shed them and grow a new set.

animals.name: Spiders
animals.fact: A spider’s eight legs attach to the front part of its body.

animals.name: Goats
animals.fact: Goats chew their food again after first swallowing it. This helps them break down tough plants.

animals.name: Snakes
animals.fact: A snake can flick its tongue to pick up tiny scent particles from around it.

animals.name: Ball pythons
animals.fact: A ball python may curl into a tight ball and hide its head when it feels threatened.

animals.name: Hamsters
animals.fact: A golden hamster can carry food in pouches inside its cheeks.

animals.name: Parrots
animals.fact: Parrots have two toes pointing forwards and two pointing backwards. These feet help them grip branches.

animals.name: Fennec foxes
animals.fact: A fennec fox’s large ears help it hear and release heat in the desert.

animals.name: Long-necked dinosaurs
animals.fact: Sauropods were plant-eating dinosaurs with long necks. Dough Mino is an imaginary dinosaur inspired by them.

animals.name: Domestic cats
animals.fact: A cat’s whiskers sense nearby objects and movement in the air.
